subject: Order form: commit floor, invoicing recipient & tax evidence
messages:
From: Danielle Harper <danielle@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lopez <t.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order form & invoice routing questions (Acme Health)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the recent order form. A couple of follow-ups from procurement before we hand this to legal / finance:

- Commit floor: the order form shows a single "minimum commit" line but no ramp. Can you confirm whether the commit floor is annual or quarterly for billing purposes? Our accounting needs explicit cadence to map to P&L.
- Invoice recipient: we need the invoice to be sent to Acme Health — Accounts Payable, Attn: Tom Lopez, with PO # when provided. Can you confirm which billing entity will appear on the invoice?
- Net terms: the document references Net 30 in the appendix; our preference is Net 45 for enterprise agreements. Is that something you can accomodate?
- Taxes & evidence: attached tax certificate here for our records. Also please confirm which party will provide tax residency evidence for withholding (if required).

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf; tax_certificate_acme.pdf

Can you loop in whoever handles commercial redlines on your side? We'd like to close this by EOD Friday.

Best,
Danielle
Danielle Harper
Procurement Manager, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com
[Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]
[Attachment: tax_certificate_acme.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Harper <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & invoice routing questions (Acme Health)

Hi Danielle — thanks, and appreciate the attachment. Quick replies inline below and looping in Ben (sales ops) and Karthik (commercials/legal liaison) to confirm redlines and the invoice entity.

- Commit cadence: Our standard is annual minimums but we can support a phased ramp (Q1 ramp + quarterly true-ups) if that helps with your P&L. Ben / Karthik — can you propose wording for a 4-quarter ramp?
- Invoice recipient/entity: We typically invoice from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity). If Acme needs a different remit-to, we can add an invoice recipient clause and map invoices to the payee name + PO #.
- Net terms: We are generally Net 30; larger enterprise deals can be moved to Net 45 with legal & finance approval. Ben — can you confirm internal approval path and any impact to pricing?
- Taxes & evidence: We'll record the tax certificate in the deal file. For withholding/residency evidence, our finance team needs the certificate up front; any recurring reverse-charge handling should be documented in the order form appendix.

I will pull together a redline and a short invoice-stub example to make the remittance explicit. Ben / Karthik — could you get a redline to Acme and an updated PDF for signature? I can follow up with DocuSign link once we have legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
[Sent from Redwood Console]

Date: 2028-12-20T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Order form & invoice routing questions (Acme Health)

Kim / Karthik — quick proposed commercial edits attached. High level:

1) Commit floor and ramp
- Add explicit quarter-by-quarter ramp: 25% of annual minimum due each quarter for Q1–Q4, with a "true-up" invoice at end of each quarter for usage above the committed level.
- Annual true-up retained as a fallback for billing reconciliation but not primary cadence.

2) Invoice recipient / remit-to
- Add an "Invoice Recipient" field in Order Form Exhibit A to map Payee entity to remit-to address and email (AccountsPayable@acmehealth.com / Attn: Tom Lopez). Invoices will include PO # if supplied.

3) Net terms
- Accept Net 45 for this arrangement pending finance approval; add clause that late-payment fees are assessed per MSA if beyond 60 days.

4) Taxes & evidence
- Redwood will accept Acme's tax certificate as sufficient residency evidence. Add a line requiring a refreshed certificate on material renewal (>12 months) or on request. For any withholding, parties will follow local law and coordinate evidence exchange; Redwood will not gross-up unless explicitly agreed in writing.

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_v3_Redline.docx

Please review and I can push the redline to Danielle with markup.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_v3_Redline.docx (DOCX, 85KB)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-21T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: FW: Order form & invoice routing questions (Acme Health)

Thanks Ben — reviewing the redline, a few clarifications from legal / procurement ops perspective:

- The quarter-by-quarter ramp language looks good. Suggest we include explicit examples (numeric) in Exhibit B so Acme's AP team has a straightforward reconciliation template.
- For Net 45: finance will approve for base commit but require CFO sign-off for prepay/advance credits; Ben, please flag if pricing needs a small uplift for Net45.
- Taxes: recommend we add a short "Tax Evidence" checkbox in the order form where Acme confirms they provided the certificate and choose the withholding responsibility option (Acme / Redwood / TBD). This avoids ambiguity at renewal.

I'll prepare a clean PDF with tracked changes removed and a one-page cover note summarizing the changes for Acme's procurement. Kimberly, if you can confirm the invoice header (Redwood Inference, Inc. vs. Redwood Inference, LLC), I'll lock the remit-to.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Commercial Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
